proof_attempt_summary: The D0 graph proved a dependent sparse-learning risk upper bound, a restricted iid packing benchmark, and a buffered phase-stacked IV/Wald transfer. A source audit replaced an overbroad coupling citation with a direct proof; a later math audit exposed an underspecified generic GMM citation, which was deleted and replaced by direct estimator and Wald algebra in the consuming theorem (main 9998bd2a0615, independently accepted). D0.5 still judged the sound package incremental: the logarithmic minimax gap and dependence-specific necessity at the blocking and sparse-Gram frontier remain open, with no bounded same-topic route to the field floor.
tldr: The primitive result is an expected independent-test risk bound for one observable coefficient-constrained best-subset estimator on the declared full-vector geometric mixing class with marginal coordinate tails: \(Cs[\sqrt{L_n/n}+a_n\log(e+a_n)L_n/n]^2\) when the sparsity times that deviation scale is small. Its iid-order upper rate \(CsL_n/n\) holds in the enlarged two-condition region \(s^2L_n\lesssim n\), \([a_n\log(e+a_n)]^2L_n\lesssim n\). An explicit random-design Fano adaptation of RWY gives \(c s\log(ep/s)/n\) on the iid subclass and, by inclusion, on the entire mixing class. The orders match only when \(L_n\asymp\log(ep/s)\). The retained simpler causal-use strip supplies the nuisance rate for a credited buffered phase-stacked IV transfer with full cross-phase HAC and honest joint Wald coverage under \(s_TL_T=o(\sqrt T)\), allowing zero pooled relevance with strong stacked relevance. The blocking elbow and logarithmic gap remain residual frontier questions.
gap: Existing dependent sparse-regression theorems inspected rely on projection-tail envelopes, joint Gaussianity, linear-process structure, additional interaction conditions, or bounded responses with a block penalty. Buffered dynamic-IV theory consequently treats the needed population nuisance rate as an input.
fill: A variance-sensitive whole-vector coupling lemma yields an iid-order expected prediction rate on an explicit sparsity--dimension strip. The classical Raskutti--Wainwright--Yu iid packing result benchmarks that rate, and a credited incremental phase-stacked orthogonal-GMM transfer converts the primitive rate into joint causal inference with full cross-phase HAC.
